title.official: Protocol to the Agreement Establishing the African Continental Free Trade Area on Digital Trade

issuer.name: Chairperson of the African Union Commission

relevance.reason: A continental digital-trade protocol whose objectives expressly include emerging and advanced technologies and which is accompanied by an Annex on Emerging and Advanced Technologies addressing AI, IoT, blockchain and related technologies. It is binding once in force, but it is not yet in force and its AI provisions are largely cooperative.
ai_provisions: Article 3 — specific objectives, including promotion of emerging and advanced technologies
Annex on Emerging and Advanced Technologies — responsible development and use of AI and other emerging technologies, regulatory cooperation, risk assessment, regulatory sandboxes
relevance.excluded_scope: Not in force; AI provisions are framework/cooperation provisions, not directly applicable product rules.

dates.notes: Adopted by the AU Assembly on 18 February 2024. Eight annexes, including the Annex on Emerging and Advanced Technologies, were adopted in 2025 according to a 2026 tralac backgrounder. Entry into force requires 22 ratifications.

status_note: Adopted but not in force. As of the September 2026 tralac backgrounder consulted, no State Party had deposited an instrument of ratification, although Nigeria's Federal Executive Council approved ratification in November 2025.

parties.summary: No ratifications deposited as of the tralac backgrounder date; entry into force requires 22 ratifications.
unknowns: Ratification status is taken from a non-official tralac backgrounder; the AU depositary record was not read.
The exact legal effect of the 2025 annexes and their adoption dates was not verified on an AU primary document.

languages.note: The AU treaty page lists English, French, Arabic, Portuguese and Spanish texts of the Protocol; the compiled annexes also include Swahili. Only English metadata was consulted, so the authentic-language clause was not verified.

sources.note: Official treaty page: adoption 18 February 2024; links to the text and compiled annexes in several languages.
